subject: Architecture
title: The Truss Bridge: Triangles of Steel
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Truss Bridge: Triangles of Steel.

hook.text: A triangle is the only shape that can't be deformed without breaking a side. Truss bridges use hundreds.

buildup.text: Steel beams arranged in triangular patterns create a framework that is both light and incredibly strong.

discovery.text: Different truss patterns — Pratt, Warren, Howe — distribute forces in different ways for different loads.

twist.text: Railroads made truss bridges famous. Thousands were built across America in the 1800s from standard kits.

climax.text: The Forth Bridge in Scotland uses 54,000 tons of steel trusses — visible engineering as architecture.

punchline.text: A shape you learn in kindergarten holds up trains.

quiz.question: Why are triangles used in truss bridges?
options: They look more attractive than squares
Triangles cannot be deformed without breaking a side
They use less paint than curved structures

details.summary: Truss bridges use interconnected triangles to distribute loads with remarkable efficiency. Because triangles cannot deform without changing the length of their sides, truss structures are inherently rigid, using far less material than solid beams while supporting equal or greater loads.
details.whyItMatters: The truss principle — that triangles are inherently rigid shapes — underpins nearly all structural engineering. Understanding trusses reveals why triangles appear in everything from roof structures and cranes to spacecraft frames.
takeaways: Interconnected triangles create inherently rigid structures
Trusses use far less material than solid beams of equal strength
The triangle principle appears throughout structural engineering

faq.question: Why are triangles so strong?
faq.answer: A triangle cannot change shape without changing the length of at least one side. Rectangles can deform into parallelograms, but triangles are locked rigid by geometry alone. This makes every member work in pure tension or compression, the most efficient use of material.

faq.question: What are the main types of truss patterns?
faq.answer: The Pratt truss angles diagonals toward the center, optimizing for steel. The Warren truss uses equilateral triangles. The Howe truss angles diagonals away from center. Each pattern distributes forces differently depending on materials and loading conditions.
